The function follows a strict sequence: measure baseline → inject → loop 3 samples → rollback → (if not aborted) measure after. Start by writing the skeleton with those 5 named steps as comments, then fill in each. `system.inject_fault(experiment_label)` and `system.rollback(experiment_label)` are the mutation calls; `system.measure_slo(n_baseline)` and `system.measure_slo(n_monitor)` are the measurement calls.

In the monitoring loop, collect each sample into a list. After each sample, check `if sample < slo_threshold`. On breach: call `system.rollback(experiment_label)`, set `report.aborted=True`, `report.abort_reason='slo_breach'`, `report.fault_period_slo=min(samples)`, and `return report` immediately. Do NOT continue sampling after a breach — you've already violated the abort condition.

When all 3 samples pass (no breach), call `system.rollback(experiment_label)` and then set `report.steady_state_after = system.measure_slo(n_baseline)`. Set `report.fault_period_slo = min(samples)` — use the minimum, not the mean, because SLOs are worst-case metrics. The `system.events` list must show `('fault_injected', label)` before `('rollback', label)` — verify with `print(system.events)` during development.
